A December 2024 motorcycle crash needed a left leg embolectomy and right hand fasciotomy, a June 2025 high-pressure paint-gun injury of the left palm needed debridement, and a June 2026 crash left a T10 Brown-Sequard syndrome now in outpatient rehab.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT / PREVENTIVE

30 yo M transferring in. His last physical was at his old primary office a couple of years back; he didn't keep up with them and wants a regular doctor he can actually reach. No complaints today.

PMH: none.
PSH: none.
Meds: none, no supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.

Family hx: father has high blood pressure, found at 58. Mother has an underactive thyroid, found at 55. Nothing else he knows of.

Social: automotive spray painter at a body shop, full time. Wears a respirator in the booth. Single. Smokes cigarettes every day. Drinks socially, 2-3 drinks a week. No drug use. Rides a motorcycle in the warm months.

ROS: negative on a full review.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet, BP fine. Comfortable, fit-appearing man. Ears, eyes, mouth unremarkable. Neck supple, no nodes. Normal S1 S2, nothing extra. Breath sounds clear throughout, no wheeze. Belly soft, nothing tender. No leg swelling. Skin clear. Moves everything well, gait normal.

A/P:
1. Preventive care, 30M. Fasting not needed: lipids, CMP, CBC drawn today. Offered one-time HIV and hep C screening, he agreed. No tetanus date on file and he can't recall one, Tdap given today. Flu shot once the fall supply is in, can do a nurse visit.
2. Cigarette smoking. Talked through why and how; he knows he should stop and isn't ready to pick a date. Went over patches, gum and the prescription options so he knows they exist. Will bring it back up next visit.
3. Works with paints and solvents. Respirator in use, nothing to add.
4. Motorcycle: helmet every ride, he says yes.

Back in a year for a physical, sooner if anything comes up.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Victor,

Everything from Tuesday's blood draw is normal: cholesterol, blood sugar, kidney and liver tests, and blood counts. The HIV and hepatitis C screening tests came back negative too. Those are one-and-done, no need to repeat unless something changes.

The nurses can do your flu shot any weekday once it arrives in October, just call or message to grab a slot.

Your primary care team

events.reason: Left lower leg pain after motorcycle crash

conditions.label: Traumatic arterial injury of left lower leg

reports.text:
ARTERIAL DUPLEX, LEFT LOWER EXTREMITY
Indication: motorcycle crash, pale painful left leg with weak distal pulses.
Technique: grayscale, color and spectral Doppler of the left lower extremity arteries.
Findings: Normal arterial flow in the left femoral arteries. In the left lower leg there is an abrupt loss of arterial flow consistent with acute occlusion, with diminished flow beyond it.
reports.conclusion: Acute arterial occlusion of the left lower leg.

documents.title: Outside ED Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE (outside hospital)
Visit: 12/11/2024, arrived 12:20 by ambulance; note 13:40

CC: Severe L lower leg pain, motorcycle crash.

HPI: 32 yo male, motorcycle crash roughly 4 hours ago. He was pinned and extrication took a long time per EMS. Main complaint is severe pain in the left lower leg. Also says his right hand got crushed under the bike. Arterial duplex of the left leg done on arrival, about an hour before this note, shows acute arterial occlusion.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father HTN, mother hypothyroidism.
SH: Former smoker, quit about 6 months ago. Social drinker, 2-3/week. Works as an automotive spray painter.

Vitals: stable, see flowsheet.

Exam:
L lower leg: swollen and pale. Pulses weak beyond the injury. Passive dorsiflexion of the foot causes severe pain. Sensation reduced over the top of the foot. Cannot move his toes.
R hand: swollen, tender, deferred to hand surgery.
Otherwise alert, airway intact, no other injury found on survey.

Labs: K 5.2. Cr 1.1. Myoglobin 150 (H). CK 2500 (H).

Imaging: L LE arterial duplex - acute arterial occlusion.

MDM: Acute limb ischemia of the left leg from traumatic arterial injury after crush and long extrication. Muscle injury with CK and myoglobin up, K mildly high, creatinine ok. IV fluids running. Vascular surgery at bedside, taking him to the OR for embolectomy. Hand surgery asked to see the right hand.

Impression: Traumatic arterial injury L lower leg with acute occlusion. Elevated CK/myoglobin.
Disposition: OR, then admit.

documents.title: Outside Operative Report - Vascular Surgery
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 12/11/2024
Preop dx: Acute arterial occlusion, left lower leg, after blunt trauma.
Postop dx: Same.
Procedure: Left lower leg embolectomy.
Anesthesia: General.

Indications: 32M after motorcycle crash with prolonged entrapment; pale, swollen left leg, weak distal pulses, motor and sensory loss in the foot; duplex with acute occlusion.

Description: Supine, prepped and draped. Exposure through a medial left leg incision. Arteriotomy made, balloon embolectomy catheter passed distally and proximally with retrieval of fresh clot. Good inflow and back-bleeding afterward. Arteriotomy closed. Completion imaging showed restored flow to the foot. Doppler signals strong in the foot at the end of the case. Wound closed in layers.

EBL: minimal. Complications: none. To recovery stable.

documents.title: Outside Operative Report - Hand Surgery
documents.author: hand surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT - HAND
Date: 12/11/2024 (fasciotomy); 12/14/2024 (closure)

Dx: Compartment syndrome, right hand, following crush injury in a motorcycle crash.

12/11: Right hand tense and swollen with pain on passive stretch of the fingers after his leg case, clinical compartment syndrome. Taken back for right hand fasciotomy: two dorsal incisions for the interosseous compartments, plus thenar and hypothenar releases. Muscle pink and contractile. Wounds left open with moist dressings, hand splinted and elevated.

12/14: Swelling down. Delayed primary closure of all incisions without tension. Splint reapplied.

No complications. Hand therapy to start after discharge.

documents.title: Outside Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/11/2024, discharged 12/17/2024

Diagnoses:
- Traumatic arterial injury of left lower leg with acute occlusion, s/p embolectomy 12/11
- Compartment syndrome of right hand from crush injury, s/p fasciotomy 12/11, delayed primary closure 12/14
- CK and myoglobin elevation from muscle injury

Course: 32M brought in after a motorcycle crash with long extrication. Left leg ischemic on arrival, duplex with acute occlusion, to the OR for embolectomy the same afternoon with flow restored. Right hand developed compartment syndrome and was released that evening by hand surgery, closed on 12/14. Aggressive IV fluids for CK 2500 and myoglobin elevation; urine output good throughout. CK 610 and creatinine 0.9 on 12/16, potassium normal. By discharge, left pedal pulses palpable, foot strength and sensation normal, walking independently. Right hand incisions closed and dry, splint for comfort.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge meds: oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325 mg 1 tab q6h prn pain, #15. No other medications.

Follow-up: hand surgery clinic in about 3 weeks for suture removal and hand therapy plan. PCP within one week. Off work until cleared by hand surgery.

Condition at discharge: good.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Phone Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Called pt day after discharge from the hospital (motorcycle crash, L leg embolectomy, R hand fasciotomy). He's home, a coworker picked him up.

Pain: taking the oxycodone about twice a day, manageable. Leg: walking around the apartment fine, no new numbness, foot warm. Hand: in the splint, dressings dry, no fever. Understands to call or go to ED for a cold or numb foot, rising hand pain, fever, wound drainage.

Med list reviewed: oxycodone/APAP only. Has hand surgery appt in early Jan. Booked with PCP Monday 12/23. Hospital records requested.

documents.title: Hospital Records Received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records received by fax from the hospital for the 12/11-12/17 admission: ED physician note, vascular and hand operative reports, discharge summary, arterial duplex and lab results. 22 pages scanned. Routed to PCP ahead of Monday's visit.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-Up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit.

32M seen for the first time since his crash on 12/11. Hospital records reviewed (ED note, both op notes, d/c summary, received 12/19). In short: L lower leg arterial occlusion after a long extrication, embolectomy same day; R hand compartment syndrome, fasciotomy 12/11, closed 12/14; CK peaked 2500 and was 610 by 12/16 with fluids, creatinine stayed normal.

Today: leg feels close to normal, a little sore at the incision. Hand stiff and sore in the splint. Using oxycodone once a day or less. Sleeping ok. No fevers.

Meds: oxycodone/APAP 5/325 prn (hospital Rx, short). NKDA.

Exam: vitals fine. Afebrile. L leg: medial incision healing, staples in, no redness or drainage. Calf soft. DP and PT pulses palpable. Foot warm, moves toes, sensation intact. R hand: splint off for exam, dorsal and palmar incisions closed, mild swelling, no drainage, fingers pink with good refill, limited flexion from swelling and pain.

A/P
1. S/p L lower leg embolectomy for traumatic arterial injury - perfusion good. Repeat BMP and CK today.
2. R hand compartment syndrome s/p fasciotomy and closure - healing. Hand surgery f/u is set for early January, they'll start therapy.
3. Pain - winding down, fine to stop the oxycodone when he's ready. No driving on it.
4. Off work until hand surgery clears him; work note given.

Will message with labs. RTC 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Labs from Monday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Victor, your muscle enzyme (CK) is back to normal and your kidney function and potassium are normal too. Nothing more to check on that front. Hope you got some rest over the holiday.

documents.title: Hand Surgery Follow-Up Letter
documents.author: hand surgery
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

I saw your patient Victor Morales today, about four weeks out from his right hand fasciotomies (12/11/2024) and delayed primary closure (12/14/2024) for compartment syndrome after a crush injury.

He is doing nicely. Incisions are fully healed, sutures out today. Swelling is minimal. He makes a near-full fist and full extension, intrinsic function is good and sensation is normal throughout. He started hand therapy last week and is working on grip and stiffness.

Plan: continue therapy twice a week. I anticipate return to full duty around mid-February; he will need to tolerate prolonged spray-gun use. I'll see him back as needed.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.

Sincerely,
Hand Surgery

documents.author: hand surgery

OPERATIVE NOTE
06/08/2025
Dx: High-pressure paint injection injury, left palm.
Procedure: Irrigation and debridement, left palm.
Anesthesia: General, upper arm tourniquet.

The entry wound was extended along the palm. Paint-stained tissue was found along the injection tract and excised until clean tissue remained. Flexor tendons and digital nerves were inspected and intact. Copious irrigation. Loose closure over the wound, bulky dressing and volar splint.

No complications. Continue IV cefazolin, elevate, early motion as pain allows.

events.reason: Right leg weakness after motorcycle crash

conditions.label: Brown-Séquard syndrome
conditions.note: Right hemicord contusion at T10, motorcycle crash

reports.text:
MRI THORACIC SPINE WITHOUT CONTRAST
Indication: motorcycle crash, right leg weakness, sensory level.
Technique: sagittal and axial T1, T2 and STIR sequences.
Findings: T2 hyperintense signal within the right half of the spinal cord at T10, consistent with cord contusion. No intramedullary hemorrhage. Cord is not compressed. Vertebral body heights and alignment are maintained; no fracture. No epidural hematoma. Posterior ligaments intact. Remaining cord signal normal.
reports.conclusion: Right hemicord contusion at T10. No fracture, compression or ligamentous injury.

documents.title: Outside ED Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY MEDICINE NOTE (outside hospital)
DOS 06/22/2026, arrival 17:45, trauma alert

CC: weak right leg after motorcycle crash.

HPI: 34M brought in after a motorcycle crash this afternoon. Known to us from crashes and a hand injury in 2024-25 (L leg embolectomy and R hand fasciotomy Dec 2024; L hand injection injury June 2025). Complains his right leg is weak and he can't feel it when it's touched.

Meds: none. NKDA.
FH: father with HTN, mother with hypothyroidism.
SH: former smoker (quit 2024). EtOH socially, 2-3 drinks/wk. Spray painter.

Vitals: see flowsheet.

Neuro: alert and oriented. Arms: full strength and normal sensation both sides. RLE strength 3/5. Proprioception and vibration diminished in the right leg. Light touch decreased on the right from T10 down. Pain and temperature preserved on the right, reduced on the left from T12 down. Reflexes normal throughout. Denies bowel or bladder incontinence.
Rest of trauma survey without injury.

Labs: CBC wnl. Lytes wnl. Tox screen negative.
MRI T-spine: right hemicord contusion at T10, no fracture.

MDM: Picture is a Brown-Sequard syndrome at T10 from a right hemicord contusion - ipsilateral weakness and dorsal column loss, contralateral spinothalamic loss two levels lower. Spine surgery consulted. Admit to trauma.

Dx: Traumatic Brown-Sequard syndrome, T10.
Dispo: admit, trauma surgery.

REHABILITATION DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 06/26/2026 - Discharge 07/17/2026 (21 days)

Rehab dx: Incomplete thoracic spinal cord injury, Brown-Sequard pattern, T10, traumatic.

Program: 3 hours a day of PT and OT. Gait training, right leg strengthening, balance work, stairs.

At discharge: right leg strength 4/5 throughout. Walks household and community distances with a single-point cane, stairs with a rail. Independent in dressing, bathing and toileting. Bladder emptying normally, no retention; bowels regular, continent. Skin intact.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medication: acetaminophen 500 mg, 2 tabs every 8 hrs as needed.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-Up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit.

34M, third serious injury in 18 months. Motorcycle crash 6/22: right hemicord contusion at T10 on MRI with a Brown-Sequard pattern, no fracture. Trauma admit 6/22-6/26, nonoperative per spine. Inpatient rehab 6/26-7/17. All records reviewed.

He walked in with a cane. Right leg tires and feels heavy by the end of the day. Feels his right foot "isn't where I think it is" sometimes. No falls. Bladder and bowels normal. Sleep ok. Mood: frustrated about being out of work, not down. Acetaminophen 1-2x/day, enough. PT eval is this afternoon.

Meds: acetaminophen 1000 mg q8h prn. NKDA.

Exam: vitals normal, weight steady. Alert, cheerful enough. Arms: normal strength, sensation and reflexes. RLE: 4/5 hip flexion, knee extension, ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion. LLE 5/5. Position sense reduced at the right great toe, vibration reduced right ankle. Pinprick and cold reduced left leg. Reflexes normal and symmetric. Walks steadily with a single-point cane. Skin intact over sacrum and heels.

PHQ-9: 4.

A/P
1. Brown-Sequard syndrome T10, traumatic, improving. Continue outpatient PT 3x/week, PM&R follow-up mid-August. Fall precautions reviewed.
2. Pain: acetaminophen as is.
3. Mood: PHQ-9 4. Normal frustration, will keep checking.
4. Work: out of work per rehab. He'll bring in the short-term disability paperwork from his employer's insurer.
5. No riding or driving until cleared.

RTC 6-8 weeks, sooner if he slips.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Victor, your form was completed and signed by your doctor and faxed to the insurer today. A copy is at the front desk if you want one.

documents.title: PM&R Clinic Letter
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

I saw Victor Morales in clinic on 08/13/2026, four weeks after discharge from our inpatient unit for an incomplete T10 spinal cord injury with a Brown-Sequard pattern (06/22/2026).

He is in outpatient PT three times weekly. Right leg strength is 4/5. He no longer needs the cane in the house and uses it outdoors and on uneven ground. Bladder and bowel function remain normal. No falls. Pain controlled with acetaminophen as needed.

Plan: continue PT with endurance and balance goals. Not yet ready for the standing and booth work of his job; we will reassess return to work in about 6 weeks. Still no motorcycle or driving.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: acetaminophen prn.

Sincerely,
Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation

documents.title: PT and going back to work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doc. PT says my leg is coming along, I did a whole session today without the cane. Rehab doc wants to wait 6 weeks on work. My shop is asking if I could come back part time to do prep and masking, not the booth. Is that something you can sign off on or does it have to be her?

documents.title: RE: PT and going back to work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great to hear about the session without the cane. Since rehab is managing your recovery and the disability claim, light duty should be cleared by them first; I'll message the rehab office to ask about part-time prep work. We'll go over it at your visit on 9/15 too.

documents.title: Message to PM&R Office
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Left a message with the rehab clinic nurse line: patient asking whether part-time prep and masking work (no spray booth) is reasonable before the planned return-to-work reassessment. Asked them to call back or update us after they decide.
